privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: What Mapsly collects, why, and the choices you have.
privacy.s1_p1: Mapsly is a local business intelligence service. We watch the public footprint of local businesses — reviews, search results, ads, websites — and turn it into a clear picture an owner can act on. This policy explains what we collect, why, and the choices you have.
privacy.s1_p2: Questions about anything here? Email support@mapsly.ai. We answer privacy requests within 30 days.
privacy.s2_heading: 2. What we collect when you visit
privacy.s2_p1: If you browse mapsly.ai or open a page we made for your business, we collect a small amount of visitor data:
privacy.s2_b1: Basic analytics — which pages and sections you view, and which buttons you click.
privacy.s2_b2: A random visitor id stored in your browser, so we can count unique visitors. It is not linked to your name or email.
privacy.s2_b3: A salted hash of your IP address, used to filter bots and abuse. We never store the raw IP.
privacy.s2_b4: Cookies needed for sign-in and language. The Cookies policy lists every one.
privacy.s3_p1: Mapsly's picture of a local market is built from public sources only:
privacy.s3_b1: Google Business listings — name, address, hours, photos, ratings, and reviews.
privacy.s3_b2: Ad libraries — the public records of ads a business runs on Meta and Google.
privacy.s3_b3: Public websites — the speed, content, and search visibility of pages anyone can open.
privacy.s3_p2: This is information anyone could look up — we organize it. If we made a page about your business and you want it gone, use the remove link on that page or email support@mapsly.ai. We take the page down and stop emailing you.
privacy.s3_p3: For businesses in the EU — including Poland — this is "legitimate interest" processing under GDPR Article 6(1)(f): we're describing your public footprint, not marketing to you. If your business is a sole proprietorship where the listing is your own name, EU law treats it as personal data, and you can object under GDPR Article 21 — the same remove link or email above stops it, no reason required.
privacy.s4_heading: 4. What we collect when you have an account
privacy.s4_b1: Account basics — your name, email address, and language preference.
privacy.s4_b2: Your business profile — the listing you claimed and the public data we refresh for it.
privacy.s4_b3: Payment details — handled by Stripe. We never see or store your card number, only a token, the last 4 digits, and the billing country.
privacy.s4_b4: Product usage — which features you use, in aggregate, so we can improve them.
privacy.s5_p1: We use this data to run the service: show your dashboard, refresh your business data, sign you in, charge your subscription, and send the emails you'd expect — your weekly check-in, receipts, security notices.
privacy.s5_b1: We do not sell or rent personal data. To anyone.
privacy.s5_b2: We do not collect patient or health information. Mapsly works with public business facts, never customer or patient records.
privacy.s5_b3: We do not use your content to train AI models.
privacy.s5_b4: Mapsly is not for children. We don't knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 16.
privacy.s6_p1: A small set of vendors helps us run Mapsly, each seeing only what its job needs: Stripe (payments), Resend and Zoho (email), DataForSEO (public business data), Anthropic (AI drafting), Sentry (error monitoring), Vercel and Neon (hosting and database).
privacy.s7_p1: Wherever you live, we honor these requests:
privacy.s7_b1: Access — get a copy of the personal data we hold about you.
privacy.s7_b2: Correction — ask us to fix anything that's wrong.
privacy.s7_b3: Deletion — close your account and have your personal data deleted.
privacy.s7_b4: Removal — have the page we made about your business taken down, via its remove link or by email.
privacy.s7_b5: Unsubscribe — every email we send has a one-click way out.
privacy.s7_b6: Portability — receive your data in a machine-readable format.
privacy.s7_b7: Objection (EU/UK) — object to processing based on legitimate interest; we honor every request, no reason required.
privacy.s7_p2: Email support@mapsly.ai from the address on your account. We may need to verify it's you before acting.
privacy.s8_p1: Account data lives as long as your account does. When you delete your account, we erase your personal data within 30 days — billing records stay as long as tax rules require. Server logs are kept for 30 days. Visitor analytics survive only as anonymous aggregates.
privacy.s9_p1: Mapsly is operated from Alberta, Canada. Our servers and service providers process data in the United States. Everything travels and rests encrypted, and access inside Mapsly follows least privilege.
privacy.s10_p1: When this policy changes, we update this page and the date at the top. Material changes get an email to active accounts 30 days ahead. For anything privacy-related:

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.subtitle: The agreement between you and Mapsly.
terms.s1_p1: By creating an account, claiming a business, or using Mapsly, you agree to these terms and the Privacy Policy. If you use Mapsly for a business or agency, you confirm you have the authority to bind it.
terms.s2_p1: Mapsly watches the public footprint of your local business — reviews, search results, ads, and website — and turns it into a clear weekly picture with the fixes that matter most. The owner plan is $29 per month. Agency plans are priced at checkout. The intelligence Mapsly provides is drawn from a shared index we build from public sources across millions of local businesses. The data you access is licensed to you on a non-exclusive basis — the same underlying public-source data may be provided to other customers; you are paying for access to Mapsly's index and analysis, not for exclusive ownership of the underlying data. Data is refreshed on a periodic cadence rather than in real time, and each lead shows when it was last verified.
terms.s2_p2: Mapsly is a monitoring and insight tool built on public data. It is not legal, medical, or financial advice.

We provide data from public sources as-is and are not responsible for how you contact anyone, or for deliverability, compliance, or reputation outcomes.
terms.s4_b4: Reverse-engineer or attempt to extract our scoring formulas or signal logic.
terms.s4_b5: Misrepresent your identity, your ownership of a business, or your affiliation with an organization.

terms.s6_p1: Mapsly's numbers come from public sources, refreshed on a schedule. They can lag reality or contain errors. If something about your business looks wrong, email support@mapsly.ai — we correct it or remove it.
terms.s7_p1: Anything you write in Mapsly — notes, pitches, custom filters — stays yours. You give us a limited license to host and display it as needed to run the service. We do not use it to train external AI models.
terms.s8_p1: Mapsly is provided "as is", without warranties. We aim for the service to be available around the clock but don't guarantee it — third-party outages can affect ours. Decisions you make from Mapsly data are yours.
terms.s8_p2: To the maximum extent the law allows, Mapsly's total liability for any claim is limited to what you paid us in the 12 months before the event. We are not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages. You are responsible for complying with every law that applies to your use of the data — including CAN-SPAM, CASL, the TCPA, FCRA, HIPAA, and GLBA — and you will indemnify Mapsly against any claim arising from your use of the data or your outreach.
terms.s9_p1: You can close your account anytime in settings. We may suspend accounts that break these terms, fail to pay, or put other users or our infrastructure at risk. After termination, your data is deleted per the retention schedule in the Privacy Policy.

cookies.title: Cookies Policy
cookies.subtitle: Every cookie Mapsly sets, and how to control them.
cookies.s1_p1: Cookies are small text files a website stores in your browser. They let us remember things between pages — like the fact that you're signed in. Mapsly sets very few, and this page lists all of them.
cookies.s2_essential_p1: Always on — without them you can't sign in or stay signed in. Your browser may show their names with a __Secure- prefix.
cookies.s2_essential_b1: authjs.session-token — keeps you signed in. Expires after 30 days, or when you sign out.
cookies.s2_essential_b2: authjs.csrf-token and authjs.callback-url — protect the sign-in flow from forgery and return you to the right page after sign-in.
cookies.s2_essential_b3: NEXT_LOCALE — remembers your language if you change it in settings. Lasts one year.
cookies.s2_essential_b4: mapsly_checkout_nonce — set for 30 minutes when you start checkout, so we know the person coming back from Stripe is the one who left. Only sent on checkout pages.
cookies.s2_analytics_p1: Mapsly sets no analytics cookies today. Our landing pages count visitors with a random id kept in your browser's local storage — it stays on our site and is never used to follow you around the web.
cookies.s2_analytics_p2: On our report pages a banner asks first. If you accept, we load two advertising tags — the Meta (Facebook) pixel and the Google Ads tag — to measure results and show relevant ads. If you decline, they stay off. No other pages load advertising tags.
cookies.s2_third_party_p1: When you pay, Stripe sets cookies on its checkout pages for fraud prevention. We don't control those — see stripe.com/cookies-policy.
cookies.s3_p1: You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Blocking essential cookies will break sign-in; everything else keeps working.
cookies.s4_p1: If we add or remove a cookie, we update this page and the date at the top.
cookies.s5_p1: Questions about cookies or anything privacy-related:

refunds.title: Cancellation and refunds
refunds.subtitle: Cancel anytime. Start free — so there's no risk to try.
refunds.s1_p1: Cancel from Settings → Billing whenever you like. No call, no form, no retention offer. Your plan stays active until the end of the period you've already paid for, then simply doesn't renew. You won't be charged again.
refunds.s2_p1: Mapsly has a free plan, so you can map a market and pull your first leads at no cost — and no risk — before you ever pay. Because of that, paid charges (subscriptions and credit top-ups) are non-refundable once made, including partial months. Cancelling stops every future charge; it does not refund a charge already made. Credits pay for the research we run or serve on a business — contacts, reviews, ads, rankings and site health. A research that comes back empty (for example, a business with no website or no reviews on file) is still a completed research and is charged: you are paying for the look, not a guaranteed result.
refunds.s3_p1: Nothing in this policy removes any cancellation or refund right you have under the consumer-protection law of your province or state. Where the law requires a refund, we honour it.
refunds.s4_p1: Any refund required by law goes back to your original payment method through Stripe, usually within 5–10 business days.

faq.title: Quick answers.
faq.q1: Where does your data come from?
faq.a1: Google Maps, Search Console, Yelp, BBB, Trustpilot, Meta Ad Library, your website (Lighthouse), Reddit, job boards, certificate transparency, WHOIS, and 20+ other sources. Everything we use is either an official API or publicly observable. No scraping behind logins.
faq.q2: Is the free report really free?
faq.a2: Yes. One full report per business, no signup required. You see your rank, top 3 gaps, and your competitor breakdown. Paid plans unlock weekly refresh, alerts, more competitor detail, and the AI review-responder.
faq.q3: How is this different from other reputation tools?
faq.a3: Most tools tell you about your own reviews. Mapsly tells you how you compare to every competitor in your city — with the names, the reasons, and the fixes. No sales call. No annual contract. Cancel anytime.
faq.q4: What cities and verticals are covered?
faq.a4: At launch: med spa, HVAC, real estate, chiropractor, vet, roofing, plumbing, auto repair. We map one market at a time and expand weekly. You can request coverage of a vertical or city from inside the product.
faq.q5: Will my data be sold to anyone?
faq.a5: We use publicly observable signals only. When you sign up as a business, you opt into our network. Agencies see your business in lead searches if you match their criteria — that's the deal that funds your $29/mo. You can opt out of agency surfacing at any time.

faq.q1: Why do signals beat a raw lead list?
faq.a1: A name is a coin flip. A signal is intent. When you can see a business losing bookings to a slow site, ignoring its reviews, and running ads with no tracking, you know exactly who to call, why, and what to open with — which is why a signal-grounded first touch replies closer to 18%+ than the 1–2% of a cold list.
faq.q2: How is Mapsly different from a contact database?
faq.a2: Contact databases sell names and emails by the seat — the same list everyone else buys. Mapsly is built on local-business signals they can't see: Google reviews, the ad libraries, search rankings, site speed, and the page's own code. You're not buying contacts; you're finding the businesses with the exact problem you fix.
faq.a3: Mapsly reads each business across our index of 2M+ local businesses — contacts, reviews, ads, rankings and site health — so you pitch with a real reason, not a guess. Leads and markets you've paid for stay saved and re-open for free.
faq.q4: Where does the data come from?
faq.a4: Public sources only — Google Business profiles and reviews, the Meta and Google ad libraries, search results, and the business's own website. We don't collect, buy, or broker private customer lists, patient records, or any non-public data.
faq.a5: Start with up to 50 free leads from markets we've already mapped — matched to your signals, with contacts ready. No card. Opening a brand-new market is a paid feature.
faq.q6: How does Mapsly compare to Apollo or Origami?
faq.a6: Apollo and Origami sell contacts; Mapsly sells qualified local businesses with the reason to call. Apollo bills per seat and is built for B2B — it's blind to most local businesses and the signals that close them (reviews, ads, site speed, rankings). Origami meters every action, so a fully-enriched lead adds up fast. Mapsly prices in whole credits — a lead's core data (contacts + site tech) is one credit, and you add reviews, speed, ads, or rankings only when a pitch needs them. Discovery is free and there's no per-seat tax — meaningfully cheaper per lead you actually work, on data neither of them computes.
